```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`qtl2mr` estimates selected-locus, founder-aware Mendelian-randomization
effects for qtl2-style multiparent data. This short walkthrough
loads a bundled fixture, prepares two loci, runs an analysis, reads its primary
estimate and warnings, and locates the shareable report.

The fixture is synthetic teaching and integration material only: it is not
independent method calibration, biological evidence, or application validation.

## Load the example

```{r load-example}
library(qtl2mr)
data("qtl2mr_example", package = "qtl2mr")
```

The fixture has 96 samples, eight founders, one chromosome, four markers, and
two selected teaching loci (`m1`, `m2`). In a real analysis, choose loci with
`qtl2mr_select_instruments()` or a prespecified list
(`vignette("from-qtl2", package = "qtl2mr")`); the `exposure_lod` column of
`marker_map` is an illustrative label, not qtl2 output.

## Prepare the input

```{r prepare-input}
resources <- qtl2mr_prepare_resources(
  allele_probs = qtl2mr_example$allele_probs,
  kinship = qtl2mr_example$kinship,
  pheno = qtl2mr_example$pheno,
  covar = qtl2mr_example$covar,
  marker_map = qtl2mr_example$marker_map,
  metadata = qtl2mr_example$metadata
)
instruments <- data.frame(exposure = "x", marker = qtl2mr_example$selected_loci)
input <- qtl2mr_pair_input(resources, instruments, exposure = "x", outcome = "y")
stopifnot(validate_qtl2mr_input(input, require_selected_loci = TRUE))
input$metadata$founder_qc_outcome$loci
```

`qtl2mr_pair_input()` adds one pair and its instruments (only `exposure` and
`marker` are needed) to the shared resources. Its founder QC, on by default,
drops a locus whose rarest founder has fewer than `min_founder_copies = 5`
expected allele copies (`E_min_y`) in the outcome's samples; both loci pass.

## Run the two-locus quick start

```{r quick-analysis, results='hide'}
result_dir <- tempfile("qtl2mr-getting-started-")
result <- run_qtl2mr_analysis(
  input,
  output_dir = result_dir,
  make_figures = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
```

`progress = FALSE` keeps the walkthrough quiet; by default each stage and a
final summary are printed. The statistical settings are fixed: the analysis
always runs the leave-one-locus-out and instrument-set sensitivity refits,
refers Q to chi-square and standardises phenotypes. The `qtl2` package is
needed only upstream or for `validate_qtl2_scan1coef()`.

## Read the result and warnings

```{r read-accessors, results='hide'}
primary <- qtl2mr_primary_result(result)
warnings <- qtl2mr_warnings(result)
```

```{r prepare-result-tables, include=FALSE}
primary_view <- data.frame(
  estimator = primary$reported_estimator,
  estimate = primary$theta_reported,
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", primary$reported_ci_lower, primary$reported_ci_upper),
  primary_reliable = primary$primary_reliable,
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

actionable_warnings <- warnings[warnings$shown_in_main_report %in% TRUE,
  c("warning_id", "severity"), drop = FALSE]
rownames(actionable_warnings) <- NULL
```

```{r read-result, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(primary_view, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(actionable_warnings)
```

The reported estimate is the Star-space second-order estimate, given only for
a numerically acceptable, bounded fit. An unresolved or unbounded fit is left
unreported; the Two-step IVW, weighted median and weighted mode comparators
remain inspectable as diagnostics. The only notice here, `no_kinship_ols`,
says that this fixture has no kinship, so the founder LMM reduces to ordinary
least squares; a later section adds one.

```{r first-stage}
first_stage <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "data", "block_first_stage.csv"))
first_stage[, c("marker", "F_X_block", "partial_R2_X_block", "partial_R2_Y_block", "steiger_pass")]
```

`weak_block_first_stage` is raised when a retained locus has F_X < 2, that is,
its founder effects on the exposure do not reach nominal p = 0.05. Both loci
are above that guide, but `m2` is close to it and explains more outcome than
exposure variance (`steiger_pass = FALSE`). The Steiger direction check refits
without `m2` and reports the result next to the primary estimate in
`data/steiger_sensitivity.csv` (about 0.79 instead of 0.89); it never filters
the primary estimate.

The estimate is in **SD of outcome per SD of exposure**; `theta_raw_units`
converts it to the original units of the fixture's `true_theta = 0.75` (about
0.93 here). A bounded fit does not guarantee 95% coverage: weak instruments,
correlated loci and same-sample selection remain limitations. `primary_reliable`
is a legacy name for this numerical check, not a claim of causal validity.

## Simulated Q p-value and bootstrap standard errors

`qtl2mr_diagnostics()` adds a Q p-value calibrated by simulation and bootstrap
standard errors for the weighted median and mode, from the stored locus blocks.
Each draw refits MR, but not the LMMs; 200 draws (default 1,000) keep this fast.

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics <- qtl2mr_diagnostics(result, nsim = 200L)
diagnostics[, c("Q_p_chisq", "Q_p_sim", "se_weighted_median", "se_weighted_mode")]
```

It is also written to `data/diagnostics.csv`; the main result is unchanged.

## Fit with a kinship matrix

The bundled fixture has no kinship. This second fit creates a nonzero kinship
from independent, synthetic background features to demonstrate the LMM input
path; it is not a reconstruction of a real mouse pedigree.

```{r kinship-example, results='hide'}
set.seed(401)
ids <- rownames(qtl2mr_example$pheno)
background <- matrix(rnorm(length(ids) * 24L), nrow = length(ids))
K <- tcrossprod(background) / ncol(background)
K <- (K / mean(diag(K)) + diag(length(ids))) / 2
dimnames(K) <- list(ids, ids)
resources_lmm <- qtl2mr_prepare_resources(
  qtl2mr_example$allele_probs, list("1" = K), qtl2mr_example$pheno,
  qtl2mr_example$covar, qtl2mr_example$marker_map
)
prepared_lmm <- qtl2mr_pair_input(resources_lmm, instruments, "x", "y")
lmm_dir <- tempfile("qtl2mr-lmm-")
lmm_result <- run_qtl2mr_analysis(prepared_lmm, output_dir = lmm_dir,
                                  make_figures = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
```

```{r kinship-hsq}
read.csv(file.path(lmm_dir, "data", "hsq.csv"))[, c("role", "trait", "hsq", "hsq_status")]
summary(lmm_result)$estimate
```

hsq is estimated by REML for each trait without the locus. Here both traits
get `hsq = 0` (`boundary_zero`, flagged by the `hsq_boundary` notice), so the
kinship term has no effect and the estimate equals the fit without kinship: a
valid boundary fit here, not evidence that kinship is unimportant in DO data.

## Combine two data sets

`qtl2mr_combine_resources()` joins two resources objects, for example two data
sets measured on overlapping mice. Here `x` is measured on the first 64 mice
and `y` on the last 64, so 32 mice have both traits.

```{r combine}
part <- function(keep, trait) {
  qtl2mr_prepare_resources(
    lapply(qtl2mr_example$allele_probs, function(a) a[keep, , , drop = FALSE]),
    kinship = NULL, pheno = qtl2mr_example$pheno[keep, trait, drop = FALSE],
    covar = qtl2mr_example$covar[keep, , drop = FALSE],
    marker_map = qtl2mr_example$marker_map)
}
both <- qtl2mr_combine_resources(part(ids[1:64], "x"), part(ids[33:96], "y"))
unlist(both$metadata$combined_resources[c("n_samples_x_only", "n_samples_y_only",
                                          "n_samples_overlap")])
```

A shared sample ID means the same mouse, so its probabilities and covariates
must agree. Each trait uses its own samples, so `qtl2mr_pair_input(both, ...)`
gives a two-sample analysis with partial overlap. Two separately genotyped
cohorts need a kinship computed on the combined probabilities; no cohort
covariate is added, as whether one is needed is your decision.

## Open the useful files

Open the report with `browseURL(file.path(result_dir, "report.html"))`. The
same folder contains `summary.md` and `data/output_manifest.csv`. Supply a
named `output_dir` in your own analysis to keep the results.

## Move to your own data

Use founder **allele** probabilities (sample x eight founders x marker),
numeric traits and covariates with sample IDs, an explicit instrument table,
and harmonized chromosome-specific LOCO kinship. The companion
`vignette("from-qtl2", package = "qtl2mr")` shows the upstream steps and
explains which choices are yours. Exposure and outcome each use their own
usable samples and their overlap is modelled. `qtl2mr_select_instruments()`
builds one instrument set per exposure, and `run_qtl2mr_batch()` fits many
pairs, each exactly as `run_qtl2mr_analysis()` would.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(result_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
unlink(lmm_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
```
